name: maybe_Field2D_Map_SetVariantCallbackB
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Map_SetVariantCallbackB(MapRoot* self, u32 arg2, MapOwner* owner, int mode, int apply)
summary: Second of the two variant-callback switchers of a 2D map node: mode 0 asks the owner's vtable +0x1C whether it is in the fallback state (playing the direction animation when it is) and then either installs the Field2D_SpriteNode callback {0x0070D2CC, 0x006720F4, self} or releases the old object at +0xA0 and rebuilds through 0x005BE5A8; mode 1 records the mode byte in owner+0x3E0 and rebuilds through 0x005BE800.
evidence: Named callees Field2D_SpriteNode_SetCallback and Field2D_Sprite_UpdateDirectionAnim plus the sibling 0x006713D4 (same mode/apply switch, same +0xA0 release) fix the family; which of the two variants a caller wants is still positional, so the B suffix and maybe_ stay.

name: Container_List_ClearAndDestroy
summary: Destroys every node of an intrusive doubly-linked list: walks the ring from list+0xC, unlinks each node through its +0x1C/+0x20 neighbours, releases the node's owned payload when the flag at +0x10 is set and frees the node.
evidence: The body is the complete unlink-and-free loop over an intrusive ring (head at list+0xC, links at node+0x1C/+0x20, payload released when node+0x10 is set), so the bulk-teardown reading is certain; the name stays generic because the container is engine-specific, not std::list, and the two callers (Ui_StatusWindow_ReleaseSlots, maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_DestroyObjectBody) only agree with it.

name: Os_IpcSendCommandWord
summary: Sends one 32-bit parameter to a service: writes the fixed request header 0x00550040 and the value into the thread-local IPC buffer (TLS+0x80/+0x84), issues svc 0x32 (SendSyncRequest) on the handle at 0x007AF0D8 and returns the response word (or the raw Result when it is negative).
evidence: The parameter is a u32 stored at TLS+0x84, not a byte, so the old 'SendByte' wording was wrong; the named callers Mem_InitializeMainHeap and Os_IpcSendByteLocked (0x00107E9C = lock, this, unlock) confirm the 'send one command word' reading. Which service the handle belongs to is still unknown.

name: maybe_Os_IpcSendResultState
summary: Calls the locked IPC send helper 0x00107E9C and normalises its Result to a two-valued state: 1 when the result is non-negative, 2 when it is negative. It is a status wrapper, not an update-mode getter.
evidence: The body is exactly Os_IpcSendByteLocked() followed by (result >> 31) + 1, the standard 'normalise a Result to 1/2' idiom; there are still no callers, so neither the owner nor the meaning of 1/2 is proven. Renamed only to follow the corrected callee name.

name: maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry
signature: int maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry(u32 dst, u32* outLen, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Drives a stack-allocated provider object (vtable 0x00780FA4) through command 0x45: queries 0x00123BAC, calls the provider's virtual +4, creates a kernel handle, then loops on 0x001228A8 with svcWaitSynchronization1 (0x24) and svcCloseHandle (0x23), retrying up to three times and copying the payload to dst.
evidence: Named callees Fs_ReadRecordBlock (0.55) and the handle helpers keep the 'read a record' reading, but the body is dominated by handle/semaphore machinery and the provider object is unnamed, so the retry/framing wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Os_ScanParamBlocks
summary: Fallback scan for a parameter entry: reads sixteen 0x40-byte blocks from offset 0x400 through Os_ReadChunkedTable, looks for a word whose low byte is 0xFE, unpacks the two 12-bit fields and the two payload words into out and returns 0; returns 0xC8810FEF when nothing matches.
evidence: Same unpacking code and windowed reader as 0x001179C0, and the return constant is the SDK error code; the record's owner is still unnamed and the only callers (maybe_Gfx_BlitWorker, maybe_Os_LookupParamEntry) are themselves guesses.

name: Os_SvcCallChecked
summary: Checked kernel/IPC call wrapper: runs the command wrapper 0x00117AB8 and, when it fails with anything other than the 'not found' class 0xFFFFFFF9, reports the Result to the SDK error handler 0x0011ED40 with the call-site address 0x001221F4. Returns the Result unchanged.
evidence: The body is fully visible: call 0x00117AB8, and when the Result is negative and its class is not 0xFFFFFFF9 report it through 0x0011ED40 with the call-site address 0x001221F4, then return the Result unchanged. The named callee Gfx_IpcCmd90000 (0.6) is the wrapped call, so 'checked call wrapper' no longer depends on the caller list.

name: maybe_Os_SvcCallCheckedAlt
summary: Second checked IPC-send helper: calls one of the two raw send wrappers (Os_IpcSendCommand0D / Os_IpcSendCommand0E, chosen by condition flags the decompiler lost), then applies the same error policy as 0x001221C0 - 0xFFFFFFF9 is ignored, any other negative Result is reported through 0x0011ED40 - and returns the raw result.
evidence: The two send wrappers are now named (Os_IpcSendCommand0D / Os_IpcSendCommand0E), which confirms the 'two-variant send + assert' shape, but the in_CY/in_ZR inputs are a decompilation artefact, so which wrapper runs is not decidable from the C and the name stays vague.

name: maybe_Field_Action_Nut_Update
summary: Command handler (cmd 8) of the 'Nut' field action: with the world action flag clear it drops f_31/f_2C, compares the owner node name with the 5-byte literal at 0x006E7552 and with "Nut_1", and on the second match plays the follow-up animation and pushes 0xFF bytes; with the flag set it re-checks "Nut_1", re-arms the 120..210 frame timer from the game RNG and stores it in f_2C.
evidence: The literals are verified in code.bin: 0x002C1114 = "Nut_1" with "Run" and "Nut" right after it, so the action name is real; but the first comparison target 0x006E7552 is code bytes, not a string, and the object's class is unknown, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Anim_PlayByNameB
summary: Second emission of the field-actor animation method: plays g_007A3C6C[self->f_313] with the entry-0 fallback, then fixes the height through 0x0066A244/0x005F7784 and clears the three bytes at f_160+0x550..0x556. Same body as 0x00182A28.
evidence: The readable bodies of 0x00182A28 and 0x001833E8 are literally identical (same table 0x007A3C6C, same f_313, same f_374 height fix, same three cleared bytes); the body also carries in_fpscr/in_s0 artefacts, so it stays a maybe_ duplicate rather than a generic animation entry point.

name: maybe_Gfx_ShutdownGlobalManagers
summary: Global teardown of six render/movie/audio helper subsystems: calls the six teardown routines 0x006B989C, 0x006B8B70, 0x006B87A4, 0x006B936C, 0x006B8F74 and maybe_Gfx_ResetGlobalPair, releases the six singletons at 0x007C835C..0x007C84BC and finally drops the object behind 0x007AE184 through its virtual +4.
evidence: The six 0x006Bxxxx teardowns and the six singleton releases are visible, and the only caller is Ui_Overlay_Shutdown, so 'global teardown' is solid; 'painters' was unsupported - the named callees are movie/VRAM/MoLive managers - hence the rename, but the six subsystems are still only identified by their addresses.

name: maybe_Ui_Anim_SetStateId
summary: Switches an animation object to another state: when the previous state word, its flag bit or the stored id is set it resets the object through 0x001DBC30 first, then stores the new state id at self+8.
evidence: The body is unchanged and self+8 is written with the new id; the reset callee 0x001DBC30 is named Ui_Overlay_Shutdown, which is a misnomer for this class's reset helper, and the callers (Gfx_Overlay_DrawSprite, Cutscene_ApplyLayoutMode, debug-menu paths) do not reveal the class.

name: Ui_SimpleWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the 0x198-byte child window: runs the base constructor, installs vtable 0x007597A4 (a subclass of the message-window vtable 0x007597F4), seeds the two default words at +0x11C..+0x124 and chains the child part constructors (Ui_NodeList_Register with id 0x12F, then the list part).
evidence: The paired destructor 0x001C3B10 is already named Ui_SimpleWindow_Dtor (0.50) and unwinds exactly the members this constructor builds, in reverse order; the caller Ui_Screen_CreateChildWindows allocates 0x198 bytes and calls this ctor, and vtable 0x007597A4 inherits the message-window dtor slots (0x50/0x54 = Ui_MessageWindow_Dtor/Delete).

name: maybe_Ui_Element2D_Ctor_vt76007C
summary: Default constructor of a small 0x130-byte 2D UI element: allocates through 0x001D8B6C, installs vtable 0x0076007C, marks the id at +0x11C as -1 (none), clears two words and installs the shared UI base vtable 0x00759378 at +0x128.
evidence: Vtable 0x0076007C carries Ui_TextWindow_BindRowPanes at +0x10 and Text_MessageStack_Pop at +0x64, so the object is a text-window class rather than a generic 'Element2D'; but the ctor is only 60 bytes and the vtable's slot 1 points inside it, so the class boundary is not clean enough to rename. Callers Ui_TitleScreen_Ctor and Ui_PresentWindow_Ctor both build text windows.

name: maybe_Ui_SenrekiWindowPart_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a sub-object of the battle-records (Senreki) window: creates the object through 0x0037E7EC, installs vtable 0x007596A0 at +0, the shared UI base vtable 0x00759378 at +0x30 and 0x00760198 at +0x38, zeroes +0x10..+0x40 and default-constructs four children at +0x44.
evidence: The caller 0x00297960 is the record-window constructor and 0x00297AE0 is Ui_SenrekiWindow_Dtor, so the parent class is fixed; vtable 0x007596A0's slot 0x10 is maybe_Ui_RowList_SwitchPage, i.e. a row-list part, but the part's own role is still only positional.

name: Actor_CreateStatusInstance
summary: Creates the large per-actor party-status instance: runs the base constructor Actor_StatusBlock_Init, stamps g_partyStatusVtable, initialises the embedded text layout at +0x23C and the 0xA7FC..0xA899 sentinels, then runs the vtable +0xBC reset and the eight-slot default loop. Returns the object base (sub-block minus 0x8F0).
evidence: The named base constructor Actor_StatusBlock_Init plus the g_partyStatusVtable stamp and the caller Menu_CreateEntryObjects fix the object as the party-status block; the twin 0x001CC3EC is the same shape for the battle-action vtable, so the 'create status instance' reading no longer depends on the caller.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_Dtor
summary: Small deleting destructor of the shop-window family: installs vtable 0x0075A78C, releases the auxiliary object at +0x10 through Ui_Window_ReleaseResources and frees the window. It is not the full teardown - the complete-object body at 0x001EB180 tears down the gold window, the two-column list and the item rows.
evidence: The address block and the +0x10 auxiliary object tie it to the shop window whose D1 body (0x001EB180) releases Ui_GoldWindow_Dtor, Ui_TwoColumnListWindow_Dtor and Ui_ItemMenu_Row_Dtor; but three different destructors exist for this family (0x001EB16C D0, 0x001EB180 D1, this one) and vtable 0x0075A78C is not cited by any named function, so the exact variant stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DeleteThunk
summary: Bare deleting-destructor thunk: stores the given vtable word in the object's first field and tail-calls the shared operator delete 0x0010F6CC. The compiler folded a self = self+0xB8-0x48-0x14-0x5C adjustment into the instruction, so the net argument is the object itself.
evidence: Nothing new beyond the now-documented meaning of 0x0010F6CC (refcounted operator delete: header at object-8, vtable+4 release), which makes 'delete thunk' safe; the owning UI class is still unknown, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_DeleteThunk
summary: Deleting-destructor thunk of the shop-window family: calls the complete-object teardown thunk 0x001EB17C (which reaches the D1 body at 0x001EB180) and then frees the object with 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The teardown target 0x001EB180 is the shop-window D1 body (it releases Ui_GoldWindow_Dtor, Ui_TwoColumnListWindow_Dtor, Ui_ThreeRowNullTextWindow_Dtor and Ui_ItemMenu_Row_Dtor), so the family is fixed; the class still rests on that body and the vtable block, not on a named reference.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionAnimObject_DtorDelete
summary: Scalar deleting destructor: runs the class destructor 0x00200220 (vptr reset plus list unlink at +8) and then the shared operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: 0x0010F6CC is now identified as the virtual operator delete, which confirms the 'deleting destructor' shape, and the cell is slot 0 of vtable 0x00769640; the class prefix Battle_ActionAnimObject is still unverified, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_SpriteActor_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field sprite-actor class: the teardown is the out-of-line 0x5646F0 thunk at slot 0, so the body is a tail call to operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The assembly (push {r4,lr}; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x10F6CC) is clear and vtable 0x76EB44 holds the 0x41F160 teardown thunk at slot 0, but the readable body is damaged (coprocessor_function, unaff_r4, UNRECOVERED_JUMPTABLE) and the class identity rests only on the 0x41F168 Run/Walk animation selector, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DtorLinked
summary: Deleting destructor for a model instance that is linked into a list: stores the class vtable 0x00782714 in the object, unlinks it from its neighbours (self[2]/self[3]) and frees the block.
evidence: Re-reading against the operator-delete callee 0x0010F6CC (header at object-8, vtable+4 release) shows the body destroys state rather than resetting it; the separate confident name Gfx_ModelInstance_Dtor already exists for another address, so this copy's class stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Script_CallbackHolder_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the small object that owns a script callback: releases the callback object with 0x005799D4 and then frees the holder with the shared operator delete 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The two-call shape is the standard deleting destructor of a small holder class once 0x0010F6CC is read as operator delete; 0x005799D4 is still unnamed, so what the holder owns (a Squirrel closure, a VM callback) is not proven.

name: maybe_Ui_FadeAnimator_DtorThunk
summary: One-call deleting-destructor thunk: hands the object straight to the shared operator delete 0x0010F6CC (header at object-8, vtable slot +4), i.e. the class has no members to destroy.
evidence: The body is a single tail call and the 'FadeAnimator' label comes only from the neighbouring maybe_Ui_FadeAnimator_InitCurve* functions, which are still maybe_; the only caller Ui_Scene_ApplyLayerFlags does not name the class either.

name: maybe_Ui_CursorIcon_Close
summary: Closes the cursor icon: drains its child list, selects the node at +0x88C, then either hides the icon through Ui_CursorIcon_Hide (for any id except 0x1F) or, for id 0x1F, stops the parent window's animation and drives the icon's vtable close slot.
evidence: The named Ui_CursorIcon_Hide call fixes the object as the cursor icon and the id-0x1F branch as a full close; the recovered body is truncated at the indirect jump (0x001D7B50), so the close slot itself is unverified and the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Menu_UpdateItemIcon
signature: void maybe_Menu_UpdateItemIcon(MenuState* self, unsigned actorId, unsigned slot, unsigned index)
summary: Refreshes one item icon/slot record of a menu page: it walks the menu's five-slot id chain (+0x4E/+0x8E/+0xCE/+0x10E/+0x14E), builds the icon name from the inline 'it_0001' sheet literal and rebuilds the slot record through Menu_ItemIcon_LoadPack / Menu_IconModel_Release.
evidence: The icon helpers are now named menu icon routines and the caller Menu_Slot_StoreActorId is the slot-claim path, so the reading holds; the body still carries an in_r12 artefact and the 'it_0001' sheet literal is the only hard naming evidence, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Menu_UpdateSkillIcon
signature: void maybe_Menu_UpdateSkillIcon(MenuState* self, unsigned actorId, unsigned skillId, unsigned slot)
summary: Refreshes a skill icon/command entry: builds the skill icon name from the inline 'sk_0155'/'sk_0034'/'sk_0104' sheet literals and updates the five-slot id chain (+0x4D/+0x8D/+0xCD/+0x10D/+0x14D) and the slot record through Menu_SkillIcon_LoadPack / Menu_IconModel_Release.
evidence: No caller and no table reference; the sibling item-icon function 0x0020BC04 is the same five-slot refresh with a different sheet prefix, so the pair reading stands, but the skill variant is still identified only by its string literals.

name: maybe_FieldParty_SubObjectDtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a FieldParty sub-object: installs the base vtable g_fieldPartyVtable, destroys the sixteen 0x58-byte entries at +0xB464 with std_destroy_range, runs the base destructor 0x00200220 and frees the object.
evidence: The vtable it installs is the named g_fieldPartyVtable (base class), not a battle-sequence vtable, so the old 'Battle_ActionSequence' attribution is unsupported; the 16x0x58 array at +0xB464 is a new detail from the body, but the derived class is still unknown.

name: maybe_FieldParty_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field-party object: stores the vtable, releases the pack handle owned at +0x125C (Pack_Handle_Dtor, then the base destructor 0x00200220 on the adjusted pointer) and frees the block. Its sibling 0x00265900 does the same teardown without the final free.
evidence: The paired non-freeing variant 0x00265900 has the same +0x125C pack-handle release, which strengthens the 'field party object teardown' reading; vtable 0x0075CCB0 still has no confidently named member, so the class stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionObject_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the action-sequence object: installs the vtable, releases the packed handle at +0x125C through Pack_Handle_Dtor, runs the shared base destructor 0x00200220 and frees the object. Its non-deleting twin is 0x0031F9F0.
evidence: The handle release is now the named Pack_Handle_Dtor (0.5) and the vtable-install/base-dtor/delete triple is identical to the unit-display destructor; the owning class is still only located by the surrounding 0x0031F3BC..0x00322DE0 block.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionObject_Dtor
summary: In-place destructor companion of 0x0031F9C4: installs the vtable, releases the packed handle at +0x125C and runs the base destructor 0x00200220, without freeing the memory.
evidence: The same named Pack_Handle_Dtor (0.5) and base destructor as its deleting twin confirm the pair; the class name still rests on the address neighbourhood, not on a vtable reference.

name: maybe_Field_InteractiveObject_DtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of a field-object class: installs the vtable, releases the packed handle at +0x497 through Pack_Handle_Dtor, runs the shared base destructor 0x00200220 on the adjusted pointer and frees the block. Same five-instruction body as 0x002658D4 and 0x0031F9C4.
evidence: The assembly is exactly push {r4,lr}; str r1,[r0],#0x25C; add r0,#0x1000; bl Pack_Handle_Dtor; sub; bl 0x200220; pop; b 0x10F6CC, so the shape is certain but the class is not. The dossier's 27 battle callers are unreliable: Battle_Update (0x0016E3E0) contains no bl to 0x003CDEB4, so the caller list cannot be used to place the class.

name: maybe_FieldParty_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of a field-party member container: installs the vtable at +0, runs the party base destructor 0x00200220 and frees the object.
evidence: Nothing new beyond the vtable-slot position 0x0075E7BC next to the field-party vtable entries; the body is the generic two-call teardown, so the class stays inferred.

name: maybe_FieldParty_DeletingDestructorB
summary: Second FieldParty deleting destructor: runs the party base destructor 0x00200220 and frees the object; same teardown as 0x0031FC40, used by the message-window derived variant.
evidence: The base teardown 0x00200220 is now documented as the party base destructor, which confirms the family; vtable 0x00763720 sits among FieldParty_InitFromParams/ResetMemberSlot, but this exact copy has no named caller so the 'B' lettering stays positional.

name: maybe_Field_ActorActionSeq_DeletingDtor
summary: Minimal deleting destructor: restores the vtable word, runs the shared base destructor 0x00200220 and frees the object; it adds no per-class teardown of its own.
evidence: Still no caller and no vtable reference of its own - only the two generic calls - so the 'ActorActionSeq' attribution remains positional (it sits before Ui_ActionSeq_ClearEntry).

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_DtorDelete
summary: Scalar deleting destructor of the battle-UI panel that owns the party member list: runs the shared base destructor 0x00200220 (which reinstalls the vtable and re-links the intrusive list at +8) and frees the panel.
evidence: Vtable 0x77BA3C slot 0 plus the member/balloon slots (maybe_Battle_Ui_Update, maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloon, Text_Window_UpdateAdvanceState) still carry the class; the body is the same generic teardown as four other panels in this batch.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_DeleteInstance
summary: Deleting destructor of a large object that embeds FieldParty at +0xB464: installs the party vtable there, clears the 0x58-byte block, runs the base destructor 0x200220 and frees the instance; the readable body is truncated at halt_baddata.
evidence: Same embedded-FieldParty reading as 0x4D2AE0 (store of g_fieldPartyVtable at +0xB464), and the 'Ui_Screen' class was only inferred from the object size; with the body truncated that cannot be confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_Cue_Finish
summary: Ends a UI cue object when its sound has finished: asks the sound system whether the handle at +0x10 is still active, then clears the handle and reloads the descriptor's callback words (+0x78/+0x7C) from 0x0072A79C.
evidence: The handle test and the HYD-descriptor callback pair are visible, but the handle helper is only maybe_Svc_Handle_IsStale and there are no callers, so both the 'Cue' and the 'Finish' wording stay inferred.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_RebuildSprite
summary: Rebuild path for the object sprite: releases the old handle, copies the stored rectangle, builds the footprint rect and re-registers the sprite as a child. The decompiled body hits bad instruction data and software_interrupt(0x24), so only the call sequence is reliable.
evidence: Control flow is damaged (halt_baddata, unaff_r4, unreachable blocks removed) and there is no confident caller; the named callees Gfx_Sprite_BuildFootprintRect and Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild only fix the sprite family.

name: maybe_Effect_CreateEightEmitters
signature: void maybe_Effect_CreateEightEmitters(int self, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Loops eight times registering an emitter/effect slot (0x0047B314 then 0x0047AF94 with the loop index) and finally enables the flag at owner+0x204 through Gfx_SpriteParts_SetFlag239.
evidence: The named callee Gfx_SpriteParts_SetFlag239 only names the final flag write; the loop body still contains a coprocessor_function artefact and lost arguments (in_s2/in_s3), so the emitter parameters and even the count semantics are unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveWindow_SetSixLabels
summary: Fills the dive window's label column: writes up to six names from the id bytes at self+0x50 through Data_LookupSubRecord, pads the remaining rows with an empty string, then writes the position counter and the page count into rows 7 and 8.
evidence: The body is fully readable: it fills up to six label rows from the id bytes at self+0x50..+0x54 (Data_LookupSubRecord per id), pads the rest with an empty string and writes the position counter and page count into rows 7 and 8. It sits in the PagerWindow cluster (immediately after Ui_PagerWindow_DeletingDtor, before Ui_PagerWindow_InitPageNumbers), but it is NOT itself a vtable slot: vtable 0x0075E1B0 slot 0x50 holds the thunk 0x0029CFA8, which branches to 0x001D6768, so whether the class is the pager window or the derived dive window is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_PagedWindow_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a window derived from the 0x00760350 class: installs the derived vtable, destroys the owned 0x18-byte element array at +0x1C (std_destroy_range, 10 elements), restores the base vtable 0x00760350 and runs Ui_Object_DtorBase plus the free.
evidence: The vtable restored at the end (0x00760350) is the class whose constructor is the confident Ui_FiveRowPagedWindow_Ctor, so this belongs to the paged-list window family; the element count is 10 in the code although the first-pass note said 12, and the derived class itself is unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_DeletingDtor_vt760350
summary: Base-class deleting destructor of the 0x00760350 UI object family: installs the base vtable, runs Ui_Object_DtorBase and frees the object. It carries no class-specific teardown, so it is the shared base slot rather than a list-window destructor.
evidence: Comparing it with the neighbouring 0x002AC854 (same base vtable, but with an owned array) shows this one does nothing except base-destroy + free, so 'Ui_ListWindow_Dtor_760350' over-specified an unnamed class; the base object identity is all the context gives.

name: maybe_Field_ActorMotion_DerivedCtorB
summary: Constructs a second derived field actor-motion object: runs the base Field_ActorMotion_Ctor, installs the derived vtable 0x0075EAD8 and returns the object.
evidence: The callee is the named Field_ActorMotion_Ctor and the caller 0x399834 is the same actor-state setup that calls 0x0028A5B4, so the two are sibling derived constructors; vtable 0x0075EAD8 carries maybe_Field_ActorMotion_AdvanceAndPickVariant at +0x08 and Ui_ListWindow_MoveSelection at +0x70, but only the vtable identifies the class, hence maybe_ and the B suffix.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_ReleaseObject
signature: void maybe_Actor_Action_ReleaseObject(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Calls the UI overlay trigger Party_Status_RequestFieldActorRefresh(core+0x48, 0), stores 0.4f in self+0xD4, then calls owner vtable+0x80() and owner vtable+0x58(owner, 4).
evidence: The vtable pair and the fixed 4 argument are the same family 0x002C0704/0x002C0D3C use, but 'ReleaseObject' is only one reading of vtable+0x58(4) and nothing in the body releases a handle.

name: Save_BuildSlotFilePaths
summary: Builds the two on-disk names of a save slot: formats "%s/Data%d" and "%s/mini_%d" with the slot number and the "data:" mount prefix, converts each narrow name to the engine's UTF-16 form and passes it to the filesystem name helper 0x00504F0C; a negative result is reported through 0x0011ED40.
evidence: The two templates are verified in code.bin: 0x002CC828 = "%s/Data%d" and 0x002CE688 = "%s/mini_%d", formatted with the "data:" prefix at 0x0072D780 (the previous pass misread them as '%s/D%atad'), and the caller is maybe_Save_LoadSlotRecords - so these are the save-slot file names, not a delete path.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteFromBounds
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteFromBounds(u32* out, GfxSceneSprite* self, int bounds, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6)
summary: Creates a scene sprite sized from a bounds record: computes the three scaled extents of the record's +0x64/+0x68, +0x74/+0x78 and +0x84/+0x88 pairs, and only when their sum is non-zero stores the caller's value at record+4 and creates the sprite instance; otherwise it clears out[0]/out[1].
evidence: The only named callee is Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance (0.5); the fixed-point divide-by-10 / divide-by-44 magic numbers that produce the extents are still unexplained, so the name keeps its maybe_.

name: maybe_Menu_ShowRowDescriptionPopup
summary: Toggles the description popup of the selected menu row: when the menu is idle and open it sets the 'popup shown' flag, closes the popup again if the sub-state at menu+0x3DE8 is 3, otherwise fills a window descriptor from the row data and shows it through Ui_MessageWindow_ShowTalkData.
evidence: The body never resolves an item record - it reads the row through maybe_Ui_Window_GetRowData, builds a 0xFFFF/0.8 window descriptor and calls Ui_MessageWindow_ShowTalkData - so the old 'consumable-item use confirm' reading was wrong; the menu class and the popup semantics are still inferred from the call sequence only.

name: maybe_Event_CameraZoomTask_Update
signature: void maybe_Event_CameraZoomTask_Update(CameraZoomTask* task, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Two-step task on a float field of the field object's attached view: step 1 saves the current value (+0x9C) into task+4, adds the delta from task+8 and flags the child; step 2 decays the delta by 0.8 per frame until it drops below 0.5 and re-applies base+delta.
evidence: The decay constant 0x3F4CCCCD = 0.8 and the 0.5 threshold are verified, and the target is (work+8)->f_54->f_20->f_210 + 0x9C (the Field_ObjectManager's attached view), but whether that value is a zoom is not confirmed. The dossier's caller list is unreliable here: 0x001D718C (Ui_OverlaySlotCtor_vt1D71DC) contains no bl to 0x00592298.

name: maybe_Ui3D_AttackSequence_Ctor_vt77B190
summary: Constructor of the 3D attack-sequence object: runs the base constructor 0x004D7124, installs vtable 0x0077B190, clears the byte at +0x45 and stores the two timing defaults 0.6f and 0.8f at +0x48/+0x4C.
evidence: The constructor is 0x38 bytes and ends exactly at 0x004E5B74, the deleting destructor installed in slot 1 of the same vtable 0x0077B190, whose slot 0x08 is Ui3D_UpdateAttackSequence - so the class is the 3D attack sequence, not a camera animation track; the 0.6/0.8 constants are only timing defaults.
